logger.warning(
    "{app}: Unexpected HTTP error: {exc}",
    app=self._app_name,
    exc=exc,

findings.fix_hint: log a sanitized form like the retry path does, e.g. f"HTTP {exc.response.status_code} {exc.response.reason_phrase}", not str(exc)
findings.problem: The old code logged only `exc.response.status_code`. The new code logs `exc` directly. httpx builds the HTTPStatusError message as "Client error '404 Not Found' for url '<request.url>'\nFor more information check: https://developer.mozilla.org/...", and that uses str(URL), which does NOT mask the password (only repr() shows [secure]). If base_url carries credentials (for example http://user:pass@host behind a basic-auth reverse proxy), they land in stderr and in log_buffer. log_buffer is shown in the web UI (triggarr/logging.py:72-82). The redacting sinks only replace the configured secret list (logging.py:38-40, 74-76), so URL userinfo is not covered. The same file deliberately avoids this pattern: the retry path at base.py:71-75 formats `f"HTTP {exc.response.status_code}"` instead of str(exc), and ConnectError says 'at configured URL' instead of printing it. That makes this a loosened data-exposure control on a changed line. The multi-line MDN suffix also clutters the single-line log format. pending: confirm the config model allows userinfo in base_url (the internal-URL exposure in the web UI applies either way).
findings.title: HTTPStatusError str() now logged: full request URL (including any userinfo) reaches logs and web-UI log buffer
findings.why_it_matters: Credentials or internal topology embedded in the URL get written to logs and shown in the web UI log viewer. That goes against the project's rule to never log secrets.

findings.problem: The old code logged only `exc.error_count()`. str(ValidationError) is a multi-line dump that includes `input_value=...` fragments of the raw /system/status response body, plus pydantic doc URLs. That untrusted upstream content now flows unredacted (only configured secrets are replaced) into log_buffer and the web UI log viewer. It also breaks the one-line-per-entry format. With a misconfigured URL pointing at some other service, the body can be arbitrary (an HTML login page, a proxy error page with internal details). pending: show that a realistic response body carries sensitive content. The confirmed effect is behavioral: multi-line, verbose log entries in the UI.
findings.title: pydantic ValidationError str() logs raw response input values into logs and the web UI
findings.why_it_matters: Raw upstream response content appears in user-facing logs. The old message was deliberately minimal.

findings.problem: This diff is a byte-for-byte revert of commit d47b4c2 ('fix(security): prevent potential key leakage in validate_connection log messages'), which had deliberately replaced `exc=exc` with structured fields (`status=exc.response.status_code`, `count=exc.error_count()`) specifically to avoid putting raw exception text into logs. The diff restores `exc=exc` at both call sites: the httpx.HTTPStatusError branch (line 233-235) and the pydantic.ValidationError branch (line 252-254), so `str(exc)` — including the full request URL for the HTTP error and per-field `input_value` detail for the validation error — now flows into `logger.warning`.
findings.title: Revert of named security fix restores raw exception logging in validate_connection
findings.why_it_matters: Two independent controls currently cover the exact concern this fix addressed: `InstanceConfig.reject_apikey_in_url` (triggarr/models/config.py:65-89) blocks an API key from ever reaching the URL, and the custom loguru sink in triggarr/logging.py is specifically built and tested (tests/test_logging.py: test_redaction_covers_tracebacks) to strip any literal secret value from the fully formatted log output, including exception text. I could not identify a concrete bypass of either control, so this is reported as a low-severity note rather than a demonstrated leak. However, it is an unexplained revert of a commit explicitly labeled as a security fix, and it does increase the amount of raw internal detail (full request URLs, validation input values) written to logs and the in-app log viewer (triggarr/web/routes.py `/partials/log-viewer`) versus the deliberately minimal fields the prior fix chose. Worth confirming this revert was intentional and re-reviewed rather than accidental.

Previously this branch logged only the status code.
